stn_including_me.accept_text:
Camp stores. Went off the stair into the water back when the mangroves still came up to the wall, and the crocolisks moved in after, which is the only reason it is still down there. Bundles, whatever is left dry inside them. Watch the toads more than the lizards. A toad out there does not look like anything at all until it is on you.

They went in at Mistvale Lagoon, south of our gate.

stn_the_stair_ends_in_a_socket.accept_text:
The stairwardens hold the middle flights and they hold them properly, in reliefs, which is not a thing I have seen a jungle troll bother to do. Get through enough of them to work past the second landing, and bring me stone. Loose course stone off the stair itself, the old grey stuff, from where it has fallen and not from where it is still laid.

The stair is Zul'Marosh Steps, east of Grom'gol on the far side of the Green Cut.
stn_the_stair_ends_in_a_socket.turn_in_text: Faces. The old stone is dressed on five faces and the new work is dressed on four, and you only leave the fifth rough if you know what is going on top of it. Whoever is laying that new course has never seen the stair finished. They are copying the outside of a thing. Three years of patient good work by somebody who does not know what it was for.

stn_nobody_left_who_built_it.accept_text:
The Rotvine call themselves keepers of that stair. They are not. They are sitting in a house calling themselves the family. Their vinespeakers carry knot-cord, which is a record, and I want them off them. I want you to hear me say that I am asking you to take a people's writing off their bodies, because I am not going to pretend to you that it is less than that.

You will find them on Zul'Marosh Steps, east of here, above the stairwardens.

stn_the_long_way_round.accept_text:
This is a favour and I am asking it as one. There is a courier pouch out on the causeway short of the fen landing, in the rot where the creepers sit. Get out to the landing, get the creepers off the ground, and look where the gangplank meets the bank. I have not reported it. I would rather go on not having reported it.

Rotvine Fen is on the far east side of the jungle, a long way from this gate.

stn_four_reports_and_a_boot.accept_text:
There is a tuber in the fen rot. Pale, about a thumb long, and it will pull water out of anything you pack it against. All of them, and they sit under the standing water, which means the toads - and a toad out there is a stone until it is on your back. I cannot condemn a boot. I can keep a foot dry inside one, and I have a ward of eleven men who would take that trade before breakfast.

Rotvine Fen. East, as far as the jungle goes before it turns to water.

stn_the_long_haul.accept_text:
No roost in a morning's flight, fine. Then we go in one hop and we go far. Over the water, up the whole length of the coast, Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad. A wyvern that flies that does not eat on the way, it eats before, and that means pressed feed, the heavy blocks, boar fat and jungle grain beaten together until it goes hard. Blocks. The rootgrubbers give you the fat. The thornbacks will try to take it back off you, because they have been robbing my feed store since the day the store existed.

Rootgrubbers and thornbacks both keep to the Green Cut, east of the gate.

stn_the_weekly_shortfall.description: Storesman Pell counts everything into Grom'gol and everything out of it, and the gap between those two numbers has been the same gap for eleven weeks. Crates, give or take one. He has written it up as spoilage twice and did not believe it either time.

stn_the_third_direction.accept_text: Coil. Strangler vine, off the wet ground where it grows green and has not gone woody yet. Cut it long and cut it fresh. Coils, and put the pythons off it before you start, because a coilvine in the canopy is exactly the colour of the thing you are reaching for and you will only make that mistake once.

stn_not_tame_fed.accept_text: Boar haunch. Not offal, not slop. Dis is not slop I be making - a raptor dat gets slop remembers it, and den she bites de hand dat brought it. Off the rootgrubbers, good ones, off the leg. And the greenpelts have found my pens, mon. Dey sit in the green by the line and dey wait on feeding hour the same as the birds do. Put dem off it before one of dem works out which end of the pen the gate is on.

stn_what_the_wood_is_for.accept_text: Battens. Thin, dressed, cut to one length. If they are dressing boards they are not burning them, and you do not build with another camp's timber unless you have run out of your own. Get me off the Stonehand, and keep the thornback apes off your back while you do it. They come down the cutline for anything that smells of the camp, and my lumber smells of the camp all the way through.

stn_a_mark_for_a_thing_still_being_made.accept_text: Two sites or the survey office files it as a special case and buries it under the stair. So: chips off the new relief work up on the Steps, the four-faced stuff and not the old grey, them. Then go and stand in the cutline camp above the fork, where somebody has been stacking our timber into something that has a shape to it. If it has a shape, it is a site, and if it is a site I have two.
